links.reason: Lines 52-55 (தன் உயிர் போலத் தழீஇ உலகத்து மன் உயிர் காக்கும் இம் மன்னனும் ... என் உயிர் காவாதது) turn Purananuru's மன்னன் உயிர்த்தே மலர்தலை உலகம் against the king; the limit-of-protection point is real.

Kural 546 is about the sceptre; verse 815 (வெற்றிலை விடினும் வேலாம், தீமை இடங்கொண்ட மனத்தினார்க்கு வென்றி இல்லை) puts victory in the mind with no sceptre or state, so the 'test case where fewer arms wins' is not in the Tamil. Shared theme of victory and virtue.
192 foretells that the lady lives and will be brought back; 196 only has her party enter the grove near Kausambi, a step in the story order rather than a fulfilment of the reading.

259 has Kattiyangaran say மன்னன் போய்த் துறக்கம் ஆண்டு ... யான் காப்பல்; 2326 says the bath is of the crowned kings' blood (அரசர் ... மண்ணுநீர்), not 'allies'', and nothing in 2326 states an incompatible claim. An ironic reversal, not a tension.

In 1663 the raft is a garland on the night sea (யாமக் கடலை நீந்துவேன்); in 380 the raft is the teacher (ஆழ்கடல் புணையின் அன்ன அறிவரன்). The word புணை is shared but 'desire's false copy of refuge' is imposed, not in either verse.
3122 has wishing-trees and creepers (கற்பகப் பொன்மரங்கள்); 3141 has the sea of senses (புலக்கடல்). No shared figure, so 'same figures' is untrue; the heaven-as-purer-bed idea is not in the Tamil.
Verse 1011 only carries a greeting (எம்வாய் ... இறைஞ்சுக); nothing in it shows Kural 685's briefness, removal of offence or smile. A shared errand-bearer topic only.
Both use the young thorn tree cut easily and hard when grown (முட்கொணச்சு மரம் முளையாகவே ... நீண்டதற் பின்), and the axe-fails detail is the verse's own. Reference to 646-648 cannot be checked here.

1316 is the next stroke of the same duel; the reversal is real but it is story sequence. Note says he cuts 'with the trident' while the Tamil has him hurl the அயில் வாள் so the thrower is cut in two with his trident.

991 line 4 (காம நோய்க்கு ஓர் அருமருந்து இல்லை) is a girl's reported saying, and 1102 a lover's remark on union; the 'stage before union' is the proposer's gloss, so no incompatible claim on the same thing.

1234 line 4 (குறவன் ... கள்ளொடூன் தேன் கை விட்டால் ஏனை எம் உடம்பு வாட்டல்) and Manimekalai 108-113 (கள்ளும் ஊனும் கைவிடின் ... உன் தனக்கு ஒல்லும் நெறி அறம் உரைத்தேன்) give the same objection; the contrast between a scaled rule and a demand to give up (இனி இவை ஒழிமின்) is real and instructive.
links.text_issue: 1234 flagged; compromise side rests on 1235 not in packet

links.reason: Verse 556 shows kings bowing and creepers clasping (அரசர் தாழ்ந்த அடிமிசை), but says nothing of his having gained himself; it illustrates Kural 268 rather than adding to it. Kings and serpents together is only a picture.

483 is Civakan's private thought (முன்னினர் முயங்கின் அல்லால் ஒவ்வாதவரை முன் புணர்தல் செல்லார்); Kural 972 speaks of worth by deeds, not of marriage order, so 'levelling stops at marriage' is imposed.

2908 (நெல்லுயிர் ... நீருயிர் ... மன்னர் ... நல்லுயிர் ஞாலந்தன்னுள்) reworks Purananuru 186's நெல்லும் உயிர் அன்றே, நீரும் உயிர் அன்றே, மன்னன் உயிர்த்தே; the epic keeps rice and water as life and adds the king, as the note says.

776 (உரு, புகழ் என்ற இரண்டு யாக்கை; புகழ் யாக்கை பின்னிற்கும்) matches the body-of-fame reading of Kural 235, but that reading of நத்தம்போல் கேடும் உளதாகும் சாக்காடும் is contested and the verse is flagged, so the explanation is a generous reading.

Both name the garland as raft (தண்ணென் மாலை புணையாக / புணையாயிற்றே), 1674 after every cooling remedy fails (சாந்தம் குளிர்செயாது); the image moves from her words to the narrator's report as the note says.

2620 has no rice or measure (உடற்றும் பிணித்தீ ... கொடுத்துண்மின்); TM 193 is a riddle of rice, pot and firebrands. Shared exhortation to give now only; the 'rice-pot image' and 'household fire' claims are not in the epic verse.
Both stubble (இருவை / இருவி) with parrots, but in AK 286 the stubble is scene, not tied to the girl; the 'image cuts both ways' teaching overreads it.
385 அறக்கதிர் ஆழி and Kural 8 அறவாழி share அறம் and ஆழி but the epic verse is about foretelling, and the Kural's ஆழி is sea in context (பிறவாழி நீந்தல்); the wheel/sea point is thin.
1973 gives the sale (ஆறு கோடி குன்றாமல் விற்றான்) with no cause; 1977 gives the sign (கடையேறும் வந்தேறலோடும் ... நிதியம் உடன் வீழும்); the later verse explains the earlier as the note says.

Both have a hen swan misled by a reflection (தண்கய நீருட் கண்ட தன்னிழல் / மதி நிழல் நீருள் கண்டு), with opposite results, which is a real contrast. The 'akam convention' the gains claim is shown by one other poem only.
130 names Ratanupura-Chakravalam; 285 names Ratna-pallavam, whose initial is garbled. Identity of the two cities is not fixed by the Tamil, so the link rests on a guess.

Kural 60 has children as ornament; Thirikadugam 64 lists three duties of a chaste wife (கற்புடையாள் பூண்ட கடன்) each earning a role, so children are not a debt owed to hold a title as the teaching says.

2451 (கூற்றம் போந்தது ... கலை சிலம்பு கிண்கிணி தாமனும் வாயினாற் சாற்றுகின்ற) and 637 (மேகலையும் வெம்முலையும் கூற்றம் ... உய்யக் கொண்டோடிப் போமின் ... கிண்கிணி) carry the same warning; moving it to the ornaments' own mouths is true.

275 is a lion hemmed at a cave mouth (முழை முகத்து இடி அரி), 1116 a lion bound with a spider's thread; but 1116's binding is the hero's own word to his parents, not seizure by the usurper, and 275 does not say he died fighting.

1706 (நோற்றல் ஒன்றோ நீளெரி புகுதல் ஒன்றோ) sets penance and fire side by side as Purananuru 246 contrasts the widow's hard life (பல்சான்றீரே ... உயவற் பெண்டிரேம் அல்லேம்) with the pyre; the epic shows both as recognised courses.

YK 248 says only good dharma ends the fruit of deeds; TM 258 has தவமறம் as the boat, and the Lord reading rests on an uncertain கேடில் புகழோன். Both name austerity and virtue as the means, so no rival account.
Kural 610 gives the ruler the earth Vishnu measured (அடியளந்தான் தாஅய தெல்லாம்), not his realm as heaven, and 1103 is a lover's question; the two books are not making rival claims on one thing.
1920 is a table of contents (வினைவெல் வகையும் ... அருந்தவன் சொன்னான்) and states no doctrine; TM 219 is a fire rite. No claim on either side to set against the other.

1919 gives a king's marriage custom (குன்றொடு காடுறை புலியனார் மகட் கோடலும்); Purananuru 336 is a refused demand and a mother's blame. Not incompatible, and the epic verse says nothing of refusal or war.
links.text_issue: line 4 ends in a doubtful word

links.reason: 2627 (இறைவி கண்ட தையா ... யானும் ஒன்றினன் துறப்பல் ... குழைந்து மெய் மறந்து நின்றான்) acts out the patikam's அரசு அஞ்சித் துறந்த ஆறு; the later verse is the scene that fulfils the early summary.

2067 has Civakan swear he be a king அறந்தலை நீங்கக் காக்கும்; Kural 560 is about cows' yield and forgotten books when the guardian does not guard. No sceptre in either, so the teaching misdescribes both; link is thin.

1814 asks that he be told her woes (தீதெலாம் எடுத்துரைத்து) and brought to her; 2325 has her eyes cool at the news of victory (வென்றி மாலை கேட்டு ... கண் குளிர்ந்த). It closes her grief, but the victory is not what she asked for.
259 (மன்னன் போய்த் துறக்கம் ஆண்டு வானவர்க்கு இறைவன் ஆக ... யான் காப்பல்) is made literal in 291 (வேந்தன் போய் விண்ணோர்க்கு விருந்தாயினானே), with the Jina's feet as his adornment as the note says.

440 proclaims the maiden as prize; 479 offers her (ஆடகச் செம்பொற் பாவை ஏழுடன் தருவல்). That is the plot keeping its promise; the 'prize passed to another' point rests on 483-484 which are not in this link.

481 promises to fill the nether world with ghee and curd; 823 brings the pots, but the herd chief is unnamed in 823 (கோன் தொறுக் காவலன்) and the identity is inferred, so 'boast paid at the next wedding' is a guess.

237 (மந்திரம் இல்லையேல் மலரும் மாண்பில; இந்திரன் இறைமையும் ... தந்திரக் கிழவர் தாங்கச் செல்லும்) shares Kural 445's idea of counsel as the ruler's support with no shared words; the extension to Indra is specific but the first gains clause is vague.

427 names Marusi as fit to speak; 517 shows an envoy angry at the king's silence (கதத்தனாகி). He has not yet said anything tactless, and his identity with Marusi is only inferred, so 'pride' is a stretch.

204 warns that power on one man makes நிலம் திரு நீங்கும்; 263 has that man's army fill the streets and surround the palace (திருநகர் வளைந்தது). It bears out the warning; 'refused' is added but the core holds.

695 uses Kama burnt by the eye-browed god and risen again as a measure of beauty; TM 346 (காமன் செயலழித்து ... யோகம்) is about restraint at Korukkai. Shared myth only; the Tirumanthiram gains nothing, and the verse is flagged.

1360 likens his leaving to the good life going (நல்லுயிர் போவதேபோல்); 1393 says parting and death belong to birth (பிரிவு சாதல்). Parting and death are named together, but 1393 does not take up the simile as claimed.

1760 is a father's sighing joy at his daughter's growth; 1762 is the council ordering the drum. That the look 'is the unspoken cause' is not in either verse and 1760 itself says no marriage is in his mind.

1118 has Kantukkatan plead that saving the girl from the king's elephant cannot be a fault (இன்னதே குற்றமாயின் குணம் யாது); Kural 550 weeding image is a fair contrast, but the sentence on the youth is not in the verse.
